issues.claim: price_ranges.full_service_or_custom: "$350-$1,500+/month, plus $499-$1,999 one-time setup at managed vendors: Sarah 24/7 from $350 ... ZAVYANS $249-$799/month plus $499-$1,999 setup ..."
issues.problem: The band's floor does not follow from the brief's own sourced prices. The list inside the "$350-$1,500+" band includes ZAVYANS at $249/month, which is below the floor, and the managed providers priced below $350 are handled inconsistently: Lithium ($179/month, managed AI answering, no setup fee) is a managed offer that is excluded from this band. One_line and inference_note repeat the same floor ("managed offers ... start at $350").
issues.fix: Restate the band from the prices actually sourced, e.g. "$179-$1,500+/month for managed/done-for-you offers: Lithium $179, ZAVYANS from $249 (+$499 setup), UpNewLevel $299/$599, Sarah 24/7 from $350 + $0.35/min, Slang.ai from $399/$599 per location, Fusion Calling Enterprise $497 (+$1,250 setup), Smith.ai Enterprise $500, Dialzara Done for You! from $1,500+", and change one_line and inference_note so the managed floor is $179-$249 rather than $350.

issues.claim: one_line and price_ranges: managed pricing is "$350-$1,500+/month plus $499-$1,999 setup"
issues.problem: Setup fees are generalised to the whole managed band when only two vendors in the set publish them. Fusion Calling publishes $799 (Pro) / $1,250 (Enterprise) and ZAVYANS $499/$999/$1,999, but Sarah 24/7 publishes Setup $0, Lithium publishes "no setup fee", and UpNewLevel includes custom setup in the plan. The implication that a managed buyer in this band should expect a $499-$1,999 fee overstates the sourced evidence.
issues.fix: Say "one-time setup observed only at ZAVYANS ($499/$999/$1,999) and Fusion Calling ($799/$1,250); Sarah 24/7, Lithium and UpNewLevel publish no separate setup fee" in one_line and in the range, keeping the inference label.

issues.claim: price_ranges.inference_note: "Ranges are the low and high published list prices observed on the vendor pages"
issues.problem: Contradicted by the band construction above: the $350 low end of the full-service band is not the lowest observed managed price ($179 Lithium, $249 ZAVYANS), so the ranges are a grouping choice, not simply the observed low/high. As written the note asserts a derivation the numbers do not support.
issues.fix: Either widen the band to the observed low managed price ($179) or reword the note to say these are hand-drawn bands per price segment, not observed minima/maxima, and list which prices anchor each boundary.

issues.claim: data_gaps: "Dialzara's Business Plus tier is listed at $199/month with the same feature checks as Pro; the vendor does not distinguish the two beyond included minutes."
issues.problem: Contradicted by the Dialzara pricing page's own comparison table, which shows Plus adding multi-agent/multi-location support, priority support (Pro: standard), unlimited knowledge-base uploads (Pro: 10), Advanced CRM via Make/Zapier/API and after-hours escalation is on both. Plus also has a 500-minute allowance vs Pro's 220.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Dialzara distinguishes Plus from Pro by included minutes (500 vs 220), multi-agent/multi-location, priority support and unlimited knowledge-base uploads; only the plan card checklists look identical."

issues.claim: Goodcall contract_terms: "free demo agent with no card and payment only when a number is connected"
issues.problem: The pricing page confirms a free demo agent and paying only when a number is connected, but does not state that no card is required (Upfirst's page does say no card; Goodcall's does not).
issues.fix: Drop "with no card" or attribute it only where the vendor says it: "free demo agent, pay only when a number is connected; no card requirement not stated".

issues.claim: buyer_reported_costs: Reddit findings — plans "around $29-$199 a month" with managed setups "around $500 a month or more", and law-firm buyers calling per-call billing "sketchy or steep at $7-$9 per call"
issues.problem: Both cited Reddit threads could not be opened (reddit.com and old.reddit.com both failed to return readable content), so neither the figures nor the stated "2026" year could be confirmed. The $29-$199 band is broadly consistent with vendor pages re-checked here (Dialzara $29, Upfirst $24.95, Rosie $49, Upfirst Premium $59.95, Smith.ai Pro $150), but the $7-$9 per call figure has no support in any source I could open.
issues.fix: Label both as unverified secondary reports, drop the year unless the thread date is confirmed, and either remove the $7-$9 per-call figure or replace it with a sourced per-call price (e.g. Smith.ai $1.67-$3.00 per call) clearly marked as list price rather than buyer report.
